question_text: Find the value of sin²52½° − sin²22½°.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Apply the sin² − sin² identity
steps.margin_note: First mark. sin²A − sin²B = sin(A+B) sin(A−B). Here A + B = 75° and A − B = 30°.
steps.memory_tip: sin²A − sin²B = sin(A+B) sin(A−B). The halves add to 75° and subtract to 30°.

recall.must_convey: That sin²A − sin²B = sin(A+B) sin(A−B) is applied, giving sin75° sin30°.
accept: use sin squared minus sin squared equals sin of the sum times sin of the difference
the halves add to seventy five and subtract to thirty
apply the identity to get sin seventy five sin thirty
identity apply cheste sin seventy five sin thirty vasthundi
write it as sin seventy five times sin thirty

steps.why: Both terms are sine squares, so this is the sin²A − sin²B form and not the mixed cos²A − sin²B form used in the previous part.
common_mistakes: Using cos²A − sin²B, which needs the first term to be a cosine.
Adding the halves wrongly and getting 74° instead of 75°.

steps.label: Substitute the exact values
steps.margin_note: Second mark. sin75° = (√3 + 1)/(2√2) and sin30° = ½. Multiply and simplify.
steps.memory_tip: sin75° = cos15° = (√3 + 1)/(2√2), and sin30° = 1/2 halves it.

recall.must_convey: That sin75° = (√3 + 1)/(2√2) and sin30° = 1/2 are substituted, giving (√3 + 1)/(4√2).
accept: sin seventy five is root three plus one over two root two
sin thirty is a half so the answer is halved
multiply them to get root three plus one over four root two
rendu values multiply cheste root three plus one by four root two
the answer is root three plus one by four root two

steps.why: 75° and 15° are complementary, so sin75° is the same number as cos15°. Both angles are positive and acute here, so the value stays positive.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the 1/2 that comes from sin30°.
